query: For an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy in its uniform, fine lamellar state, whose strength and plasticity remain below industrial application requirements, what single intervention could improve performance for fasteners exposed to extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosive conditions? State the proposed intervention, mechanism, predicted outcome relative to the starting alloy, applicable operating and test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit falsification criteria.

generation.hypothesis: A controlled post-solidification thermal-aging treatment will induce nanoscale intermetallic precipitates along the lamellar interfaces in the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy, thereby enhancing its strength, ductility, creep resistance, and corrosion resistance under extreme temperature fluctuations and long-term load conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: Uniform, fine lamellar eutectic AlCoCrFeNi2.1 high-entropy alloy
generation.intervention: A single-step thermal-aging treatment performed at an intermediate temperature (for example, 600–700°C) for a defined period, followed by controlled cooling
generation.conditions: The treatment is designed to be applied post-solidification; the fasteners are assumed to operate under temperature cycles roughly from -50°C to 500°C with sustained mechanical loading and exposure to corrosive environments (e.g., salt-laden atmospheres)
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of stable nanoscale intermetallic precipitates at or near the lamellar interfaces
generation.mechanism: The precipitates are expected to act as barriers to dislocation motion (precipitation strengthening) and stabilize the interface structure, thereby mitigating creep and inhibiting microstructural coarsening during thermal cycling; additionally, a modified interface may reduce sites vulnerable to corrosion
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the untreated alloy, the thermal-aged alloy will exhibit higher yield strength and an improved balance between strength and ductility, along with enhanced resistance to room-temperature creep and better corrosion performance under cyclic thermal conditions
generation.baseline: Performance metrics of the as-solidified uniform, fine lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy under standard mechanical and corrosion tests
generation.boundary: The improvements are anticipated under operating conditions similar to typical fastener applications (i.e., temperature fluctuations from about -50°C to 500°C, long-term mechanical loads, and moderate corrosive exposure). Outside these limits (for example, at extremely high temperatures or in aggressive chemical environments), the beneficial effects may not be maintained
generation.uncertainty: The magnitude of mechanical improvement and optimum aging parameters require experimental validation. There is also uncertainty regarding potential over-aging, where excessive precipitate coarsening might lead to embrittlement or a reduction in ductility

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy samples in the uniform fine lamellar state. Subject one set to the controlled thermal-aging treatment (e.g., treatment at 600–700°C for a predetermined time such as 4–8 hours, followed by controlled cooling) while keeping another set as untreated controls. Simulate actual fastener operating conditions by exposing both groups to cyclic thermal fluctuations, long-term mechanical loads, room-temperature creep tests, and corrosive environments (e.g., a salt spray chamber).
measurements: Tensile testing to assess strength and ductility
Creep tests at room temperature over extended durations
Corrosion resistance assessment (e.g., salt spray or electrochemical methods)
Microstructural analysis using TEM/SEM to confirm precipitate formation and distribution
Thermal cycling tests to evaluate microstructural stability
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the thermal-aged samples do not demonstrate statistically significant improvements (or show deterioration) in yield strength, ductility, creep resistance, and corrosion resistance compared to the untreated controls, or if the treatment induces over-aging effects such as precipitate coarsening leading to embrittlement, then the hypothesis will be considered falsified.
